name: Remainder and factor theorems
formula: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + P(a), \qquad (x - a) \mid P(x) \iff P(a) = 0
whenToUse: Find the remainder of a polynomial divided by a linear factor without long division, test a possible root, or get the sum of coefficients from $P(1)$.
example: The remainder when $x^{50} + 3x + 1$ is divided by $x + 1$ is $P(-1) = 1 - 3 + 1 = -1$. The sum of the coefficients of $(x^2 - 3x + 3)^{9}$ is $P(1) = 1^{9} = 1$.
pitfall: Dividing by $x + 1$ means $a = -1$, not $+1$. Dividing by a quadratic leaves a remainder of degree up to $1$, which takes two evaluations to find.
